title: Relative-strength ratio breakout vs the other two pairs, hourly rotation long
rule_summary: Closed 1h candles. For traded pair X, let Y be the geometric mean of the closes of the other two pairs; ratio R(t) = close_X(t)/Y(t). ENTRY at close of bar t (fill next open) when: R(t) > SMA(480) of R; R(t) is the highest R close of the last 120 bars (including t); close_X(t) > SMA(480) of close_X; no position open. EXIT at close of bar t (next open) when R(t) < SMA(48) of R, or close_X(t) < SMA(480) of close_X. Hard stop 6% below entry. After an exit wait 12 bars. All signals hourly; no daily data.
mechanism: Capital rotates between large caps in waves: when one coin starts outperforming the basket, flows from momentum traders, and slow spreading of news across pairs, keep that leadership going for days. The counterparty is the holder who sells a leader too early or an arbitrageur who underprices persistent leadership. A leadership run lasts days and a move of several percent, well above the 0.35% cost, and the exit waits for ratio weakness so winners run.
